title: Pinched simplices give a weakly equivalent mapping resolution
statement:
Use simplicial categories [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting], and quasicategories, weak homotopy equivalences and right mapping spaces [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Define $\mathfrak C[\Delta^m]$ to have objects $0,\ldots,m$ and, for $i\leq j$, mapping set the ordinary nerve of the inclusion poset of subsets of $\{i,\ldots,j\}$ containing $i,j$, with empty mapping set for $i>j$ and union as composition. Monotone maps act by images of subsets. Put $\mathfrak C[S]=\operatorname{colim}_{\Delta^m\to S}\mathfrak C[\Delta^m]$ in simplicial categories. Put $J^n=(\Delta^n\star\{y\})\amalg_{\Delta^n}\{x\}$, where the join is $\Delta^{n+1}$ with last vertex $y$ and the whole initial face $\Delta^n$ is collapsed to $x$. Set $Q^n=\mathfrak C[J^n](x,y)$; monotone maps of initial faces make $Q$ a cosimplicial simplicial set. For $K$ a simplicial set define $|K|_Q=\int^{[n]\in\Delta}K_n\times Q^n$, the quotient of the coproduct of copies of $Q^n$ by the simplicial and cosimplicial identifications. Define $(\operatorname{Sing}_QT)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(Q^n,T)$. These functors are adjoint by evaluation. There is a natural cosimplicial map $p:Q\to\Delta^\bullet$ inducing a weak homotopy equivalence $p_K:|K|_Q\to K$ for every simplicial set $K$. For every Kan complex $T$, the evaluation counit $e_T:|\operatorname{Sing}_QT|_Q\to T$ is a weak homotopy equivalence.

For a quasicategory $S$ and vertices $x,y$, there is a natural weak homotopy equivalence
$$\theta_{S,x,y}:|\operatorname{Map}^{R}_S(x,y)|_Q\longrightarrow\mathfrak C[S](x,y).$$
Here an $n$-simplex of $\operatorname{Map}^{R}_S(x,y)$ is a map $J^n\to S$ sending the displayed vertices to $x,y$. On the corresponding copy of $Q^n$ the map $\theta$ is the mapping-set map induced by $\mathfrak C[J^n]\to\mathfrak C[S]$. All these maps commute with simplicial operators and maps of the displayed inputs; $Q^0=\Delta^0$ and the maps in degree zero take the displayed vertex to itself.
